reviewer: AI game tester / experienced digital-card-game UX critic
independence: No other reviewers' ratings or findings were read. This is an AI review perspective, not a recruited human critic.
scope: Current Vantage Point development preview; one 28-turn match ending by deliberate in-UI concession, plus lobby/deckbuilder exploration. Score is for this preview experience, not a competitive balance certification or shipped 0.2.1.

rating.rationale: A coherent, functional local Netrunner table with useful card inspection and explicit action costs. However, a visibly obstructed lobby selector, ambiguous access ordering, and interaction-test pilots that can lack essential matchup tools make it difficult to recommend as a polished play experience. Stability was strong in this match.

game.reasonForConcession: After initial rig development, successful central pressure, tags/identity cleanup and reaching 3 points, both centrals became protected by code gates. This interaction pilot has no decoder and no stealth credit source for Baker's bypass. Continuing a pass-only deckout would add little playtest value. This is a player concession, not an engine blocker.
game.strategy: Installed Borrowed Goods, removed its tag with Vic, ran Archives to enable Carmen's install discount, installed Carmen/Cleaver, tried Overclock on a scoring remote, probed self-trashing Event Horizon, pressured exposed HQ and R&D, installed Rotary, inspected public cards/access choices, checked Archives. Bounded DOM loops handled repeated legal run/access/continue choices and later playback skipping.

explored: Deck and character selection; matchup library
Tune deck; influence/program filters; full-resolution preview
Overclock target selection and encounter options
Central and remote runs; successful and ended runs
Access-order selection; full accessed-card inspection; stealing agendas

findings.title: Sticky lobby actions obstruct both deck selectors at the initial desktop scroll position
findings.reproduce: Open the Vantage lobby at 1280×800, scroll to document top. Both deck selectors lie behind the sticky action bar.
findings.recommendation: Keep the action bar below the deck setup or reserve explicit space; test the lobby with long deck descriptions and Resume visible.

findings.title: The full-card Vic pilot lacks a decoder and stealth funding for its own Baker cards

evidence.notice: Development benchmark and playtest list; tune the economy and card ratios before drawing balance conclusions.

findings.impact: The warning is honest but does not make missing tool coverage obvious before play. My match eventually met Tocsin code gates with no matching breaker; Baker could not supply a practical redirect without stealth credits.
findings.recommendation: Separate interaction-test pilots from curated play decks and add deck health hints (ice coverage, economy, unsupported synergies). Do not present this as evidence of competitive deck balance.

findings.title: Facedown access choices do not identify hand/deck cards versus installed server-root cards clearly

evidence.result: Selecting 'Facedown card · HQ' accessed installed Flagship, not the random HQ hand card I expected.

findings.recommendation: Use 'Random card from HQ' and 'Unrezzed card in HQ root'; keep hidden identity concealed while exposing legal zone information.

findings.title: Unavailable breaker panels and empty windows occupy disproportionate decision space

ui: Carmen: Cannot break this ice; wrong type; disabled Break all · 5 credits
Cleaver: Cannot break this ice; wrong type; disabled Break all · 6 credits
evidence.accessWindow: No additional ability choices in this window. Use the continuation below when ready.

findings.recommendation: Compact unavailable breakers to one reason, hide irrelevant price quotations, and prioritize the active continuation. Preserve the clear explicit 'Finish accessing' label.

findings.title: Action quotes emphasize money and clicks more than non-monetary consequences
findings.evidence: I installed zero-credit Borrowed Goods, then needed to clear its installation tag through Vic. The printed card explains it; the install quote itself focused on 1 click / 0 credits.
findings.recommendation: Where the engine can quote a guaranteed extra consequence, surface a brief 'takes 1 tag' annotation alongside the install cost. Treat this as onboarding help, not a rules bug.

strengths: Distinct Corp/Runner presentation and restrained teal/gold palette
Public hand counts, clicks, credits and agenda totals are available together
Full card art and text work from lobby, builder and accessed-card context
Influence filters explain in-faction versus imported cards
Character switching shows both keep-cards and starter consequences, with a working cancel
Wrong-ice-type guidance is explicit and prevents erroneous breaker activation
Explicit Finish accessing / run phase trail are useful
No game crash or engine diagnostic in 304 recorded choices
limitations: One match and one reviewer perspective; no statistical balance conclusion.
Routine legal DOM-click loops assisted repeated central run/access steps; no engine state injection or direct engine choose calls were used for browser gameplay.
Pre-concession state was reconstructed afterward from exact recorded choices with version checks and zero native errors.
Desktop screenshots worked; the attempted mobile resize had not applied before the final read, so mobile visual quality was not evaluated.
No source edits or fixes were made during this review.
